name: Vivienne Westwood
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Westwood was a primary school teacher and had only briefly attended Harrow Art College before meeting Malcolm McLaren in 1965. Her first boutique 'Let it Rock' opened in 1971 at age 30, and her first catwalk show was in 1981 at age 40.
family_context_summary: Born to a factory worker and cotton weaver in Glossop, Derbyshire; family ran a sub-post office and moved to north-west London in the late 1950s.
evidence_summary: Westwood was born into a working-class family in Derbyshire and trained as a primary school teacher. She briefly attended Harrow Art College but left after one term. She did not begin her fashion career until meeting Malcolm McLaren in 1965 at age 24, and her first shop opened in 1971 at age 30 — well after age 26.

name: Hines Ward
milestone_by_age_26: Recorded his first 1,000-yard NFL receiving season in 2001 (94 receptions, 1,003 yards, 4 TDs) and was selected to his first Pro Bowl at age 25 with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
early_history_summary: Ward was a multi-position star at the University of Georgia (1994-1997), playing quarterback, tailback, and wide receiver while earning All-SEC honors. He was drafted by the Pittsburgh Steelers in the third round of the 1998 NFL Draft and became a starter by his second season, reaching 1,000 receiving yards in his fourth year.
family_context_summary: Born in Seoul, South Korea to an African American U.S. Army father and a Korean mother; father abandoned the family early, and his mother raised him in the Atlanta area.
primary_early_advantage_tags: SEC football, multi-position versatility, athletic scholarship, single-parent adversity
evidence_summary: Ward grew up in a biracial household in the Atlanta area after his father left, raised by his Korean mother. He became a prep football star at Forest Park High School and earned an athletic scholarship to the University of Georgia, where his versatility across multiple positions (QB, RB, WR) built deep football knowledge. Drafted by the Steelers in 1998, he reached 1,000 receiving yards and a Pro Bowl by age 25. His multi-position college experience was a key leverage point.
starting_point: Born in Seoul, South Korea to an African American U.S. Army father and a Korean mother; father abandoned the family, and his mother raised him in the Atlanta, Georgia area.
current_position: Wide receivers coach at Arizona State University; retired from NFL in 2011 after 14 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers including 2 Super Bowls and a Super Bowl MVP.

trajectory.event: Enrolled at the University of Georgia on an athletic scholarship, beginning a versatile four-year college career across multiple offensive positions.
Drafted by the Pittsburgh Steelers in the third round (92nd overall) of the NFL Draft.
Recorded first 1,000-yard receiving season (94 catches, 1,003 yards) and earned first Pro Bowl selection.
Won Super Bowl XL with the Steelers and was named Super Bowl MVP.
Retired from the NFL after 14 seasons with 1,000 career receptions and 12,083 receiving yards.
Serving as wide receivers coach for Arizona State University football.

name: Izabel Goulart
milestone_by_age_26: Contracted as a Victoria's Secret Angel in 2005 at age 21, appearing in the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show and on covers of Marie Claire France and Vogue Brazil the same year.
early_history_summary: Discovered at age 14 while grocery shopping with her mother in São Carlos, Brazil. She moved to São Paulo to begin modeling, then briefly to France, before returning to São Paulo in 2001 at age 16 to join agency Success. Her career was launched by Ney Alves, and she quickly escalated to major fashion shows and campaigns.
family_context_summary: Born in São Carlos, São Paulo, Brazil, of Portuguese and Italian descent; she has four brothers and one sister. Her family was working-class and she was bullied in school for her skinny build.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early discovery, São Paulo fashion market, Brazilian model wave, VS Angel contract
evidence_summary: Goulart was discovered at 14 by a hairstylist while shopping with her mother in her small hometown. She moved to São Paulo to pursue modeling, joining agency Success at 16. The Brazilian model wave of the early 2000s provided a structural tailwind. By 21, she was contracted as a Victoria's Secret Angel, a career-defining milestone. Her family was working-class with no documented fashion industry connections.
starting_point: Born in São Carlos, São Paulo, Brazil to a working-class family of Portuguese and Italian descent; one of six siblings.
current_position: Continues to model internationally; known for work with Armani Exchange, Victoria's Secret, and Sports Illustrated Swimsuit; in a long-term relationship with Kevin Trapp.

trajectory.event: Discovered by a hairstylist while grocery shopping with her mother, prompting a move to São Paulo to begin modeling.
Returned to São Paulo and joined agency Success, launching her professional fashion career under Ney Alves.
Contracted as a Victoria's Secret Angel and appeared in the VS Fashion Show; also landed covers of Marie Claire France and Vogue Brazil.
Became the face of Armani Exchange, replacing Alessandra Ambrosio in three seasonal campaigns.
Featured in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue, expanding her mainstream visibility.
Made her final Victoria's Secret Fashion Show appearance after 12 consecutive shows.

name: Jean-Paul Belmondo
milestone_by_age_26: Starred as Michel Poiccard in Jean-Luc Godard's Breathless (À Bout de Souffle, 1960), filmed when he was 26, which made him a major international star and the face of the French New Wave.
early_history_summary: Born into an artistic Parisian family, Belmondo trained at the Conservatoire of Dramatic Arts from age 20 to 23, performing in provincial theater. After minor screen roles in the late 1950s, his breakthrough came with Breathless in 1960, which launched him as France's leading New Wave actor.
family_context_summary: Born in Neuilly-sur-Seine, an affluent Paris suburb; father Paul Belmondo was a leading academic sculptor and professor at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux Arts; mother Sarah Rainaud-Richard was a painter.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a renowned sculptor and professor at the Beaux Arts; mother was a painter, providing an artistic family environment and access to Parisian cultural circles.
primary_early_advantage_tags: sculptor father, Parisian art world, Conservatoire training, French New Wave, Godard collaboration
evidence_summary: Belmondo was born into a prominent artistic family in Neuilly-sur-Seine; his father was a celebrated sculptor and professor at the Beaux Arts, his mother a painter. He trained at the Paris Conservatoire of Dramatic Arts for three years, building classical acting skills. The French New Wave movement provided a structural wave, and his casting in Godard's Breathless at 26 made him an international star. His family's cultural capital and Parisian art-world connections gave him early access to the theatrical and film ecosystem.
starting_point: Born in Neuilly-sur-Seine, an affluent Paris suburb, to Paul Belmondo, a renowned academic sculptor and professor at the École des Beaux Arts, and Sarah Rainaud-Richard, a painter.
current_position: Died on September 6, 2021 at age 88 in Paris; final role was in 2016. Remembered as one of France's most iconic actors.

trajectory.event: Enrolled at the Conservatoire of Dramatic Arts in Paris, beginning formal acting training.
Completed Conservatoire training, receiving an honourable mention after a controversial jury incident.
Starred in Jean-Luc Godard's Breathless (À Bout de Souffle), becoming the face of the French New Wave and an international star.
Starred in That Man from Rio, becoming a major box-office draw and stuntman in commercial action films.
Won the César Award for Best Actor for Itinéraire d'un enfant gâté, which he famously refused.
Suffered a stroke that largely ended his acting career, though he made occasional appearances thereafter.
Made his final film appearance, concluding a career spanning over 80 films.
Died on September 6, 2021 at his home in Paris.

name: Seiji Ozawa
milestone_by_age_26: Won first prize at the Besançon International Competition for Young Conductors in 1959 at age 23, leading to study at Tanglewood (Koussevitzky Prize 1960) and appointment as assistant conductor of the New York Philharmonic under Leonard Bernstein in 1961 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in Japanese-occupied Manchuria, Ozawa moved to Japan at age 9 and began piano study. He switched to conducting at 15 after injuring his fingers, studying under Hideo Saito at the Toho School of Music. He traveled to France in 1959 and won the Besançon competition, launching his international career.
family_context_summary: Born to Japanese parents in Mukden, Manchuria; father was a dentist and pan-Asian activist, mother was a Christian who introduced him to Western church music. Family returned to Japan when he was 6 and struggled financially post-war.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a dentist with political connections; mother introduced Western church music; older brother became a church organist, providing early musical exposure.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hideo Saito mentorship, Toho School, Besançon competition, Tanglewood, Bernstein, Karajan
evidence_summary: Ozawa grew up in a modest family in post-war Japan; his father was a dentist but the family struggled financially. He began piano late (age 7) and switched to conducting at 15 after a finger injury, studying under the influential Hideo Saito at the Toho School of Music. His mentor's guidance led him to the Besançon competition, which he won at 23, opening doors to Tanglewood, Bernstein, and Karajan. The mentorship pipeline was the dominant early advantage.
starting_point: Born in Mukden, Japanese-occupied Manchuria to Japanese parents; father was a dentist and pan-Asian activist, mother a Christian who introduced him to Western music; family returned to Japan when he was 6 and struggled financially.
current_position: Died on February 6, 2024 at age 88 in Tokyo; served as music director of the Boston Symphony Orchestra for 29 seasons (1973-2002), the longest tenure in the orchestra's history.

trajectory.event: Began studying conducting under Hideo Saito at the Toho School of Music in Tokyo.
Won first prize at the Besançon International Competition for Young Conductors in France, launching his international career.
Won the Koussevitzky Prize at Tanglewood and began studying with Herbert von Karajan in Berlin.
Appointed assistant conductor of the New York Philharmonic under Leonard Bernstein.
Became music director of the Boston Symphony Orchestra, a position he held for 29 seasons.
Stepped down as BSO music director and became music director of the Vienna State Opera.
Died on February 6, 2024 in Tokyo.

name: Jerry Falwell
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Thomas Road Baptist Church in Lynchburg, Virginia in June 1956 at age 22 with 35 members, and launched the 'Old Time Gospel Hour' radio/TV ministry the same year, building a rapidly growing megachurch.
early_history_summary: Falwell grew up in Lynchburg, Virginia, the son of an agnostic entrepreneur/bootlegger father and a devoutly religious mother. He attended Baptist Bible College in Springfield, Missouri, graduating in 1956, and immediately returned to Lynchburg to found his own church at age 22.
family_context_summary: Born in Lynchburg, Virginia; father was an entrepreneur, bootlegger, and agnostic who died when Falwell was 15; mother was devoutly religious. Twin brother Gene also entered ministry.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a flamboyant entrepreneur with multiple service stations, bus lines, and oil businesses; no direct religious domain transfer. Mother's religious devotion influenced Falwell's spiritual path.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Lynchburg roots, Baptist Bible College, radio/TV ministry, entrepreneurial family, postwar religious revival
evidence_summary: Falwell grew up in Lynchburg with an agnostic, entrepreneurial father who died when he was 15, and a devoutly religious mother. He attended Baptist Bible College in Springfield, Missouri, and returned home to found Thomas Road Baptist Church at 22. He immediately launched a radio ministry, showing early distribution instincts. The postwar American evangelical movement provided a structural wave. His father's entrepreneurial background may have influenced his approach to building a church and media empire.
starting_point: Born in Lynchburg, Virginia to Carey Falwell, an agnostic entrepreneur and former bootlegger, and Helen Beasley, a devoutly religious mother; twin brother Gene was born 20 minutes later.
current_position: Died on May 15, 2007 at age 73; founded Liberty University and Thomas Road Baptist Church, and co-founded the Moral Majority.

trajectory.event: Founded Thomas Road Baptist Church in Lynchburg, Virginia with 35 members and launched the 'Old Time Gospel Hour' radio/TV ministry.
Founded Lynchburg Baptist College, which later became Liberty University.
Co-founded the Moral Majority, a major political organization that mobilized conservative Christian voters.
Liberty University achieved full accreditation, solidifying Falwell's educational empire.
Died on May 15, 2007 in Lynchburg, leaving a legacy as one of the most influential evangelical leaders of the 20th century.

name: Nasser Al-Khelaifi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Al-Khelaifi was a modest professional tennis player with a career-high singles ranking of No. 995, representing Qatar in Davis Cup with a 12-31 singles record. His success came as PSG president from 2011 onward, well after age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Doha, Qatar to an Arab family; befriended the future Emir of Qatar, Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, through tennis when they were teenagers.
evidence_summary: Al-Khelaifi was born in Doha and became a professional tennis player, but his playing career was undistinguished — he reached a career-high ranking of No. 995 and had a 12-31 Davis Cup singles record. His notable success came entirely after age 26, when he leveraged his friendship with the future Emir to become a major sports executive, becoming PSG president in 2011. No material tennis milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Roger Pingeon
milestone_by_age_26: Finished 8th overall in the 1966 Tour de France at age 25, his second year as a professional with the Peugeot team, demonstrating Grand Tour contender potential.
early_history_summary: Pingeon grew up on a farm near the Jura Mountains and was a cross-country skier before taking up cycling at 17. After military service in Algeria delayed his start, he turned professional with Peugeot in 1965 and immediately showed promise, finishing 8th in the Tour de France in his second season.
family_context_summary: Born in Hauteville-Lompnes, Ain, France, the fourth of five sons in a farming family. Grew up in a rural mountainous area near the Jura.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; farming family with no apparent cycling background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Peugeot team, Jura mountains, late start, Grand Tour debut, farming family
evidence_summary: Pingeon grew up on a farm in rural eastern France, the fourth of five sons. He discovered cycling as a teenager after initially pursuing cross-country skiing, and military service in Algeria delayed his professional start. He turned pro with the Peugeot team in 1965 at age 24-25 and immediately showed Grand Tour potential, finishing 8th in the 1966 Tour de France. His late start and rural background meant limited early advantages, but joining a top professional team provided the elite pipeline that accelerated his career.
starting_point: Born in Hauteville-Lompnes, Ain, France, the fourth of five sons in a farming family in a rural mountainous area near the Jura.
current_position: Died on March 19, 2017 at age 76 in Beaupont, France; final role was as a cycling consultant for Radio Télévision Suisse (1979-1998).

trajectory.event: Began cycling after discovering the sport through local club members in Hauteville, initially overcoming a heart arrhythmia diagnosis to obtain a racing license.
Completed two years of military service in Algeria, delaying the start of his professional cycling career.
Turned professional with the Peugeot-BP-Michelin team, making his Tour de France debut.
Finished 8th overall in the Tour de France, establishing himself as a Grand Tour contender.
Won the Tour de France general classification, the defining achievement of his career.
Won the Vuelta a España and finished 2nd overall in the Tour de France behind Eddy Merckx.
Retired from professional cycling after a 10-year career.
Died on March 19, 2017 at his home in Beaupont, France after a heart attack.

name: Ricardo Bofill
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Taller de Arquitectura in Barcelona in 1963 at age 23, and by 26 had completed multiple apartment buildings (Nicaragua 1964, El Sargazo 1964, Bach 28 1965, Bach 4 1965) and begun the Barrio Gaudí housing project in Reus.
early_history_summary: Born into a Catalan bourgeois family of builders, Bofill started designing at 19 with a house in Ibiza (1960). After being expelled from the Barcelona architecture school for political activism, he studied in Geneva, then returned to Barcelona to found his architecture workshop in his father's construction business premises.
family_context_summary: Born into a prominent Catalan bourgeois family in Barcelona; father Emilio Bofill was an architect, builder, and developer who worked with figures like José Luis Sert and Antonio Bonet; mother Maria Levi was an Italian Jewish arts patron.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an architect-builder-developer whose firm was sought after by avant-garde architects; Bofill literally grew up in his father's construction business and had 'the advantage of being able to start designing very young.'
primary_early_advantage_tags: architect father, construction business, Catalan bourgeois, early design start, Barcelona architecture scene
evidence_summary: Bofill was born into a prominent Catalan bourgeois family; his father was an architect-builder-developer whose firm was highly sought after, and his mother was an Italian Jewish arts patron. He grew up immersed in construction and design, starting his first project at 19. The Taller de Arquitectura was founded in 1963 in his father's business premises, giving him immediate access to construction infrastructure and professional networks. This family-domain apprenticeship was the dominant early advantage, providing both capital safety and domain proximity from childhood.
starting_point: Born in Barcelona, Spain to Emilio Bofill, an architect-builder-developer, and Maria Levi, an Italian Jewish arts patron; raised in a Catalan bourgeois family with deep construction-industry roots.
current_position: Died on January 14, 2022 at age 82; led Ricardo Bofill Taller de Arquitectura for nearly 60 years with over 1,000 projects in 50 countries.

trajectory.event: Completed his first architectural design, a single-family summer house in Ibiza, while still a student in Geneva.
Founded Ricardo Bofill Taller de Arquitectura in Barcelona, initially hosted in his father's construction business premises.
Completed first apartment buildings (Nicaragua, El Sargazo) and began the Barrio Gaudí housing project in Reus.
Completed Kafka's Castle apartment building and the Barrio Gaudí district, establishing his signature style.
Completed La Muralla Roja in Calpe, one of his most iconic works, later inspiring film sets and video games.
Expanded to France, taking on major housing projects including Les Espaces d'Abraxas in Paris.
Died on January 14, 2022 in Barcelona, leaving a legacy of over 1,000 projects worldwide.

name: Ratko Janev
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Janev completed his master's degree in 1965 and started at the Boris Kidrič Institute of Nuclear Sciences, but his PhD (1968), formation of the Atomic Collision Theory Group (1972), and IAEA appointment (1986) all came after age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Sveti Vrach (Sandanski), Bulgaria in 1939; moved to Yugoslavia during youth, attending high school in Skopje.
evidence_summary: Janev was born in Bulgaria and moved to Yugoslavia, attending high school in Skopje before studying at the University of Belgrade. He graduated in 1963, earned a master's in 1965, and began work at the Boris Kidrič Institute. However, his defining scientific achievements — his PhD (1968), forming the Atomic Collision Theory Group (1972), and heading the IAEA's Atomic and Molecular Unit (1986) — all occurred after age 26. No independently notable milestone by 26 was found.

name: Regine Heitzer
milestone_by_age_26: Won her first of seven consecutive Austrian national figure skating titles at age 16 in 1960, also winning European Championship silver and competing at the 1960 Winter Olympics; by 26 she had an Olympic silver medal (1964), two European titles (1965, 1966), and multiple World Championship medals.
early_history_summary: Heitzer first competed in World and European Figure Skating Championships in 1958 at age 14. By 16, she dominated Austrian figure skating, winning seven consecutive national titles (1960-1966) and accumulating 11 European and World Championship medals before turning professional in 1967.
family_context_summary: Born in Vienna, Austria; her family owned an upholstery fabrics wholesale business in downtown Vienna, which she later took over after her skating career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family owned a wholesale upholstery fabrics business in Vienna; no documented skating-specific family background, but the family business provided financial stability.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Vienna skating club, early international competition, Austrian national dominance, European championships, Olympic medal
evidence_summary: Heitzer was born in Vienna and began competing internationally at 14, suggesting early and intensive training. She skated for the WEV (Wiener Eislaufverein) club in Vienna, a traditional figure skating center. Her family's wholesale business provided financial stability that supported her athletic career. By 16, she won the first of seven consecutive Austrian titles and European silver, demonstrating exceptional early specialization. Vienna's figure skating ecosystem and her family's resources enabled sustained high-level competition throughout her teens and early twenties.
starting_point: Born in Vienna, Austria; family owned an upholstery fabrics wholesale business in downtown Vienna, providing a middle-class background.
current_position: Retired; took over the family upholstery fabrics business and converted it to a furniture store before retiring in 2010; awarded Decoration of Honour in Silver for Services to the Republic of Austria in 1996.

trajectory.event: First competed in World and European Figure Skating Championships, beginning her international career.
Won first of seven consecutive Austrian national titles, European Championship silver, and competed at the 1960 Winter Olympics (7th place).
Won World Championship bronze and European Championship silver, establishing herself as a consistent medalist.
Won Olympic silver medal at the 1964 Innsbruck Winter Olympics behind Sjoukje Dijkstra.
Won her first European Championship title and World Championship silver.
Won her second European Championship title and third consecutive World Championship silver.
Turned professional, skating for Vienna Ice Revue and Holiday on Ice.
Retired from skating due to a knee injury, transitioning to the family business.

name: Ryu Seung-min
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Olympic gold medal in men's singles table tennis at the 2004 Athens Olympics at age 22, defeating Wang Hao of China in the final and 1992 Olympic champion Jan-Ove Waldner en route.
early_history_summary: Ryu started playing table tennis at age 7-8 at his uncle's table tennis hall in Incheon, South Korea. His parents moved to support his training, and he won national elementary school championships. By his late teens, he was winning Asian Junior Championships and competing at the Olympics (2000 Sydney), reaching world No. 2 ranking by September 2004.
family_context_summary: Born in Seoul, South Korea; father ran a fast food restaurant and had health problems; maternal uncle ran a table tennis hall where Ryu first played. Parents gave up their restaurant to support his table tennis career and moved for training access.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct table tennis family background, but maternal uncle operated a table tennis hall and recognized Ryu's talent, providing early access to the sport. Parents made significant sacrifices, including relocating and changing careers, to support his training.
primary_early_advantage_tags: uncle's table tennis hall, early start age 7, parental sacrifice, Korean national team, penhold specialist, Olympic gold
evidence_summary: Ryu grew up in a modest family in Seoul and Incheon; his father quit his job due to health problems and ran a fast food restaurant. Ryu discovered table tennis at his uncle's hall at age 7-8 and showed immediate talent. His parents made significant sacrifices — giving up their restaurant and relocating — to support his training. He transferred schools multiple times to access better table tennis programs. By his teens, he was winning national and Asian junior championships. The Korean national team system and Samsung Life club provided elite-level training and competition infrastructure. His Olympic gold at 22 was the culmination of 15 years of intensive, specialized practice.
starting_point: Born in Seoul, South Korea to a family of modest means; father ran a fast food restaurant after quitting his job due to health problems; maternal uncle operated a table tennis hall where Ryu first played at age 7-8.
current_position: Member of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) since 2016; ITTF Foundation Ambassador; former Vice-Chair of the IOC Athletes' Commission; highest world ranking was No. 2 (September 2004).

trajectory.event: Began playing table tennis at his uncle's table tennis hall in Incheon, showing immediate natural talent.
Won the Asian Junior Championship in both singles and doubles, emerging as a top junior prospect.
Competed at the Sydney Olympics, finishing 4th in doubles.
Won gold in men's doubles at the Busan Asian Games, plus silver in team and mixed doubles.
Won Olympic gold medal in men's singles at the Athens Olympics, defeating Wang Hao in the final; reached world No. 2 ranking.
Won Olympic team bronze medal at the Beijing Olympics.
Won Olympic team silver medal at the London Olympics, his final Olympic appearance.
Became a member of the International Olympic Committee (IOC).
